discussion_comments.comment_body: Please make the artifact tool depend on a storage contract in core rather than a required cloud session ID and authenticated HTTP transport. As written, an ordinary local core session cannot use this feature: publication always requests a cloud-session upload policy, and retrieval has the same dependency. Keep signed policies, storage uploads, and signed-URL caching in a cloud implementation; provide local persistence/retrieval through the same contract and exercise the shared tool with both implementations. Merely moving this file or exporting it from the core root would leave the cloud dependency intact.

Fixed in 0b6e96f80b. `skip` and `unskip` now act on `action.itemId`: the named row is kept out of later sets for the rest of the turn and the next row fills the gap; `unskip` restores it into view from any set served this turn. Ids from another turn, or not in the pool, are refused as stale.

Fixed in e8f733f68c. A row's id is now built from the revision of the turn's first set, so it keeps that id all turn. Each new set still gets its own revision. After skipping Review, Wrap up keeps its id, and the desktop's highlight stays on it. Use, Send, Skip and Undo skip name a row by that id. Only refresh still needs the current revision, because its `more` cause names no row. The per-turn revision list was dropped, and a test pins the stable ids.

Callers pass the name of a field as a string: `"statusWriteQueue"` or `"compactionStateWriteQueue"`. The call site does not say what the string does, and the compiler accepts the wrong string. This is the problem with a boolean parameter, one step removed. Please pass the getter and setter for the queue instead, or give each queue its own small method over one shared body.
Done: `enqueueStatusWrite` and `enqueueCompactionStateWrite` each hand a getter/setter pair for their queue to one `chainWrite`. No strings.

Suggestion: make the visibility filter unconditional and drop `mcpApps` from `CreateMcpToolsOptions`.

The spec says the host MUST NOT list tools whose visibility doesn't include `"model"`, with no exception for hosts that haven't advertised the apps extension. A tool tagged `visibility: ["app"]` is never meant for the model, so hiding it when apps are off is still the right behavior (there's no app around to call it either).

That leaves the client factory flag as the single switch for MCP Apps, and removes the "the two must be set together" caveat from DOC.md. Conformant servers only send `_meta.ui` tools after the client advertises the capability anyway, so the factory flag is the real gate.

Not blocking, approving as is. It's just cheaper to collapse this now than after the option is in the published `@cline/core` surface. Feel free to make the change and I can re-review.
Hey! I went this way so as not to break the existing interface, but you're right; it's probably better to do so now rather than later.

Similar to feedback on your other PR, I suggest using a string union here instead of a boolean. Booleans often are not flexible enough to model what is going on, and tend to proliferate. Then you get a lot of booleans where a subset of the states are invalid and it gets confusing and hard to test.

Fixed in 4d4cfc1d2. The Hub protocol has no command to change a running session's model, so updateSessionModel is removed from CloudSessionHost. The lifecycle already treats a host without it as unable to switch, and the composer keeps naming the model the sandbox was started on.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Agreed, this one's worth closing in the PR: the hub now accepts `displayPrompt` on input, so it should carry it back out. @dakjdakd — could you forward `displayPrompt` in the two event copies (`session-event-projector.ts` `pending_prompt_submitted` case and `HubRuntimeHost`'s `session.pending_prompt_submitted` case)? No shipped host hits this path today, but a field that goes in and never comes out is a trap for the next integrator.

Fixed in e6dd0b4.

Both submitted-event copies now forward `displayPrompt`: the server's `pending_prompt_submitted` projection into the Hub envelope, and `HubRuntimeHost`'s conversion back into a Core event. The expanded model prompt, delivery mode, image/file arrays, and attachment count are preserved alongside the original display text.

The regression sends a Core submitted event through the real server projector and HubRuntimeHost event handler and checks both payloads. It covers a separate display string, an explicitly empty display string, and an omitted field. The Hub runtime, run-handler, and pending-prompt suites pass (58 tests), the SDK build and Core typecheck including smoke checks pass, and the changed files pass Biome.

The PR is still Draft because GitHub does not grant my account permission to mark it ready for review. Could you mark it ready from the repository side once you've checked this follow-up?

🟢 **bug** (low)

The value sent in the `X-Task-ID` request header changed from the task ID to the ulid while the header name (and therefore the contract the Cline backend sees) stayed the same. If the backend treats this header as a task identifier (attribution, rate limiting, server-side joins), the meaning of the header silently changed; for tasks that have no ulid the header is also now empty where it previously always carried a value. This is probably intended as part of "ulid everywhere", but the header name no longer describes its content.

**建议**: Confirm with the backend owner which identifier this header is expected to carry, then either keep sending the task ID or rename the header (e.g. `X-Task-ULID`) so the contract stays unambiguous. If both ids are needed, send them as separate headers.

**证据**: `"X-Task-ID": this.options.ulid || "",`
